best_existing.name: Codex follow-up queue (CLI Tab to queue, IDE extension queue mode, desktop app queue list)
best_existing.covers: Native queue in Codex: a queued message waits until the current run finishes; the IDE extension defaults to queue (chatgpt.followUpQueueMode) and the desktop app lets users edit, reorder or delete queued items.

best_existing.name: Claude Code built-in message queue
best_existing.covers: Enter while Claude works queues messages, but plain messages are passed in as soon as the current tool calls finish within the same turn; only slash and shell commands wait until the turn ends.

best_existing.name: codecShivam/claudeq
best_existing.covers: Side-pane queue for Claude Code built on Stop/SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit hooks; delivers one queued message per turn in order, no patching.

best_existing.name: Vesely/cmux-claude-queue
best_existing.covers: Option+Enter queues a prompt delivered as a fresh turn after the Stop hook fires (macOS + cmux only).

best_existing.name: ivanarama/PromptPilot
best_existing.covers: Background task queue for Claude Code and other AI CLIs with web UI and Telegram bot.

best_existing.name: coding-by-feng/ai-agent-session-center
best_existing.covers: Dashboard for Claude Code and Codex sessions with prompt queues and workspace resume.

shortcomings.what: VS Code extension request to queue instead of interrupting is still open with no maintainer reply; users ask whether it is on the roadmap.
Task-queue request still open; earlier queue issues were auto-closed by the stale bot; the cmux workaround needs macOS and cmux.
Claude Code merges queued messages into one combined turn instead of one message = one turn FIFO.
No setting to hold queued messages until the turn completes instead of folding them mid-turn.
Desktop Code tab has no way to queue a message until the turn fully ends; Ctrl+Enter interrupts.
Queued messages are never delivered in Claude Code desktop (silent loss of input).
Public criticism (Sep 2026) that Claude Code cannot queue a message as a separate next task; cites a cycle of partial fixes and regressions.
Codex queue bugs: 'App-server queued follow-up no longer exists' errors, queued prompts behaving like steer and being sent simultaneously, prompts disappearing before entering the queue.
Codex queued prompts behave like steer prompts; multiple queued prompts sent simultaneously.
Codex VS Code extension: submitted prompts randomly disappear before entering the queue.

note: Codex ships a real next-turn queue (with bugs), but Claude Code's native queue folds messages into the running turn and the desktop/VS Code surfaces cannot hold a message for the next task; third-party hook-based queues exist but are tiny, platform-limited projects.

best_existing.name: Gemini CLI interactive shell (node-pty) and tools.shell.inactivityTimeout
best_existing.covers: Setting tools.shell.enableInteractiveShell runs commands in a PTY so vim, REPLs and prompts work; inactivityTimeout kills a shell command after N seconds without output.

best_existing.name: Gemini CLI interactive shell announcement
best_existing.covers: Announces PTY-backed interactive commands in Gemini CLI (v0.9.0).

best_existing.name: Claude Code Bash timeouts and background time limit
best_existing.covers: BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (2 min) / BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS (10 min) cap foreground commands, which then move to the background; unattended sessions (-p, SDK, CI, cloud) get a 30-min/2-h background time limit (v2.1.285+).

best_existing.name: wonderwhy-er/DesktopCommanderMCP
best_existing.covers: MCP server giving the agent terminal control including long-running and interactive processes it can start and interact with.

best_existing.name: nickgnd/tmux-mcp
best_existing.covers: MCP server letting the agent drive tmux sessions (send keys, capture panes) for interactive programs.

best_existing.name: yiwenlu66/PiloTY
best_existing.covers: PTY-control MCP server so agents can operate interactive terminals like a human.

shortcomings.what: Claude Code's built-in Bash tool still has no PTY/interactive support; feature request open with no maintainer reply, users rely on tmux workarounds.
Scheduled (unattended) Claude Code task hangs indefinitely on its first Bash tool call with no timeout and no error.
Commands that hit the Bash timeout keep running in the background unbounded; agents re-run them and processes pile up.
Bash run_in_background ignores timeout and a never-exiting background task produces no notification.
Docs: local terminal, desktop and VS Code sessions have no time limit on background commands, and timed-out foreground commands are moved to the background rather than killed.
Gemini CLI still lacks a general per-tool-call timeout setting (only shell inactivity timeout); request open.

note: Gemini CLI has PTY interactive shell and an inactivity timeout, and PTY/tmux MCP servers exist (Desktop Commander is popular), but Claude Code's native shell still has no PTY and open reports show unattended sessions hanging and timed-out commands left running.

best_existing.name: Claude Code auto-continue at usage limit (autoContinueAtUsageLimit, v2.1.234)
best_existing.covers: Interactive CLI sessions (and a Desktop checkbox) wait out a claude.ai 5-hour limit and resume with a continuation prompt after reset; on by default for subscribers.

best_existing.name: Claude Code auto-continue caveats write-up
best_existing.covers: Documents surfaces and limits of the built-in auto-continue (CLI default on, Desktop checkbox, /rate-limit-options fallback).

best_existing.name: saaranshM/unsnooze
best_existing.covers: Resumes Claude Code, Codex CLI and other agent sessions when 5-hour or weekly limits reset; reads reset timestamps and runs codex resume.

best_existing.name: terryso/claude-auto-resume
best_existing.covers: Shell wrapper that waits for the Claude CLI usage limit to lift and resumes the task.

best_existing.name: songyb111-gachon/codex-auto-resume-windows
best_existing.covers: Resumes the same conversation in the Codex desktop app on Windows after usage-limit resets.

best_existing.name: dujunyi416/claude-nightshift
best_existing.covers: Quota-aware automation: queue prompts overnight and auto-resume interrupted sessions on reset.

shortcomings.what: Codex has no native auto-resume at limit reset; request open with no maintainer reply; Goals stay in usageLimited after reset until a new user message.
Codex /goal auto-resume after 5h/weekly reset requested and still open; users rely on third-party desktop scripts.

Claude Code auto-continue does not apply to -p headless or background sessions, does not auto-wait for weekly resets more than 24h away, needs Enter after >30 min laptop sleep, ends if the terminal closes, and re-arms at most twice.
Claude Code auto-continue never arms when Remote Control is connected.
Claude Code auto-continue at usage limit does not trigger.
Session stalls on a consent prompt when a model-specific weekly limit is hit instead of continuing.
Third-party wrapper fails if already over a session limit, and broke when Claude's limit message format changed.

note: Claude Code now auto-continues interactive sessions at 5-hour resets, and many wrappers cover Codex and headless runs, but Codex has nothing native and the Claude feature excludes headless/background runs and long weekly waits, with open reports of it not triggering.

best_existing.name: Claude Code Notification and Stop hooks
best_existing.covers: Hooks fire when Claude needs input or finishes, so users can trigger desktop/phone alerts or log timestamps.

best_existing.name: Claude Code Remote Control push notifications
best_existing.covers: 'Push when actions required' and 'Push when Claude decides' send phone pushes via the Claude app when blocked on a prompt or when a long task finishes.

best_existing.name: Codex tui.notifications / notify config
best_existing.covers: Maintainer describes tui.notifications with OSC 9/BEL and the notify script hook on agent-turn-complete; desktop app has OS completion notifications.

best_existing.name: tuchg/Lucarne
best_existing.covers: Notifications plus approve/resume for Codex and Claude Code sessions from anywhere.

best_existing.name: DevinoSolutions/anotifier-for-claude-codex-cursor
best_existing.covers: Desktop and phone (ntfy) notifications for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Cursor, with native VS Code support.

best_existing.name: wyattjoh/claude-code-notification
best_existing.covers: macOS desktop notification hook with sounds for Claude Code events.

best_existing.name: Riplexa Timestamps (VS Code extension)
best_existing.covers: Shows timestamps inline in the Claude Code and Codex VS Code chat panels.

shortcomings.what: No per-message timestamps in Claude Code; request open; the only third-party option covers the VS Code panel only and patches its webview.
Second open request for message timestamps in the interactive conversation view.
Claude Code VS Code extension lacks native system/toast notifications when Claude needs attention.
Codex IDE extension has no audible signal; notify hook does not fire on approval requests; third-party notifiers fail over Remote SSH.
Codex VS Code extension does not request attention when approval is required.
Claude Code Notification hook fires with a ~10 second delay.
idle_prompt notification timeout is not configurable.
Remote Control pushes need a subscription, both toggles on, a live Remote Control session and an open terminal; not available with API keys or cloud providers.
Codex Remote Control push notifications not delivered on iOS.

note: Completion and needs-input alerts are well covered by hooks, Codex notify settings, Remote Control pushes and many third-party notifiers, but IDE surfaces still lack native signals and per-message timestamps remain unshipped outside a VS Code-only patch.

best_existing.name: Claude Code per-subcommand permission matching and read-only cd
best_existing.covers: Compound commands are split on &&, ||, ;, | etc. and each subcommand matched; cd into the working directory counts as read-only; 'don't ask again' saves one rule per subcommand; /permissions lists every rule and its source file.

best_existing.name: Claude Code auto mode (classifier approvals)
best_existing.covers: A classifier decides most permission prompts instead of the user, reducing stalls in unattended runs.

best_existing.name: ldayton/Dippy
best_existing.covers: PreToolUse hook that parses bash and auto-approves commands known to be safe.

best_existing.name: oryband/claude-code-auto-approve
best_existing.covers: Auto-approves compound Bash commands by parsing pipes, chains and subshells and checking each segment.

best_existing.name: vosslab/codex-code-permissions-hook
best_existing.covers: Codex permission hook that decomposes compound shell commands and applies allow/deny TOML rules.

shortcomings.what: Permission prompt triggers on cd instead of the real command in compound statements; most-reacted permission bug still open.
Permission matching described as fundamentally broken (30+ issues, user-level rules not applied, deny-rule bypasses); community hook reimplementations have no security review.
Skills and subagents do not inherit user-level permissions.
Bypass/skip-permissions broken in versions after v2.1.77.
Remote Control mobile app shows permission prompts despite --dangerously-skip-permissions.
Quoted-characters-in-flag-names warning cannot be disabled.
Codex requires per-project trust approval; maintainers announced trusting all directories then reversed the decision and reopened the issue.
Gemini CLI workspace .gemini/policies/*.toml files do not take effect.

note: Claude Code now documents per-subcommand matching and offers auto mode, and hook-based approvers like Dippy exist, but the core issues (cd prompts, user rules not applied, subagent inheritance, bypass prompts, Codex trust, Gemini workspace policies) remain open across vendors.

best_existing.name: Claude Code repository-shared plugins, marketplaces and claude.ai synced org plugins
best_existing.covers: enabledPlugins/extraKnownMarketplaces in committed .claude/settings.json and plugin dirs under .claude/skills reach every collaborator; plugins bundle skills, agents, hooks, MCP and LSP servers; org-required plugins sync from claude.ai (v2.1.273+).

best_existing.name: intellectronica/ruler
best_existing.covers: Applies one versioned set of rules to all coding agents from a repo.

best_existing.name: dyoshikawa/rulesync
best_existing.covers: CLI generating rules, commands, subagents, MCP and other config for many agents from one source.

best_existing.name: nicepkg/vsync
best_existing.covers: Syncs MCP servers, skills, agents and commands across Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode and Codex from one config.

best_existing.name: spxrogers/agentsync
best_existing.covers: Syncs agent configs from one canonical, committable source.

shortcomings.what: Org skills still uploaded one by one in the admin console with no version history or repo link; request open.
Claude Code plugins cannot bundle rules.
Project settings.json is not inherited from a monorepo parent directory.
Docs: a repository-root plugin in .claude/skills does not load when the session starts in a subdirectory, and cloud sessions do not add repo-listed marketplaces.
Codex lacks repository-scoped marketplace and plugin configuration.
Codex plugins cannot include agents.
Codex config.toml mixes portable preferences with machine-local trust entries.
rulesync declarative sources cannot install commands, subagents, MCP servers, hooks or permissions.

note: Claude Code plugins and repo-scoped settings plus sync tools like ruler and rulesync cover much of the need, but org skills from git, rules in plugins, monorepo inheritance and Codex repo-scoped plugins/portable config remain open.

best_existing.name: taylorwilsdon/google_workspace_mcp
best_existing.covers: Google Workspace MCP server (Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs...) with multi-account operation selected per call by user email.

best_existing.name: Wh1isper/mcp-email-server
best_existing.covers: Multi-account IMAP/SMTP email MCP server.

best_existing.name: evolsb/claude-code-google-workspace
best_existing.covers: Multi-account Google Workspace and Slack MCP setup for Claude Code.

best_existing.name: majiayu000/mcp-mux
best_existing.covers: Multiplexes several accounts of one MCP server (Gmail, Slack, Notion) into one toolset with an account argument, for Claude Code and Codex.

best_existing.name: Duplicate custom connector URL trick and ProxyLoom
best_existing.covers: Adding the same MCP URL with a unique query string as a second custom connector authorizes a second account; ProxyLoom hosts connectors whose tools take an account argument.

best_existing.name: Codex Gmail multiple connected accounts (partial)
best_existing.covers: Users report Gmail now allows connecting several labeled accounts.

shortcomings.what: Built-in connectors in Claude and Claude Code on the web still allow one account per connector; request open with no maintainer reply; the URL trick does not work for the built-in GitHub connector or the web, and self-hosted multi-account servers are described as cumbersome.
Newer open requests (Oct 2026) still ask for more than one Google account per claude.ai connector.
Codex Gmail multi-account has no account selector when invoked, and other connectors lack equivalent support.
google_workspace_mcp multi-account stdio mode discards refreshed tokens, causing spurious re-auth.
Slack multi-workspace MCP servers found are essentially unused (0 stars), so coverage beyond Google/email is thin.

note: Third-party MCP servers (notably google_workspace_mcp) and a custom-connector URL trick allow several accounts per service, but vendor connectors still bind one account, Codex Gmail support lacks a selector, and multi-account coverage outside Google/email is thin and fragile.
